newsitem.title: UK: Thames to spend extra 150 mln stg investment.
newsitem.headline: Thames to spend extra 150 mln stg investment.

text.p: Thames Water Plc said on Tuesday it planned an extra 150 million stg in investment on services, unveiling the news in its interim results which showed pretax pre-exceptional profits up 15 percent at 188 million stg.

The half year results for the six months ended September 30 reported profits in line with expectations and a dividend payout of 11.2 pence, up from 9.2 pence. Thames also said the extra investment would supplement its 350 million stg annual spending to improve service standards.
The extra cash will be spent over a five-year period on various projects, said chairman Sir Robert Clarke.
These include work to cut leakage of water, cutting sewer flooding and bringing forward plans for a new reservoir.
Thames also reported that its balance sheet had been restructured following its 10 percent share buyback on July 31 and the repurchasing of 44 percent of convertible bonds for cancellation.
The utility group said that the premium paid on the share buyback and the associated tax charge of 45 million stg were charged against reserves.
The interim results were described by Clarke as "an excellent first half."
During the period operating margins rose to 33.7 percent, up 2.6 percent on the same time last year.
Gearing was up to 39 percent from 30 percent.
In a divisional breakdown of the results, utility operations saw profits rise by eight percent. Non-regulated activities swung to a nine million profit from a three million loss.
This unit embraces international contracts, products and property to insurance.
Thames Water expects international business to "contribute significant profits next year."
Looking ahead, Thames said it expects "success to be sustained in the second half."
